sources.title: Crimea

proposedOverrides.summary: Atlas-audited guide to Crimea from White defeat through the first collectivization drive, 1920 to 1930.

batchIdentityNotes: The exact south-russia feature is one Crimean polygon, not a map of southern Russia and not a modern territorial claim.
Historical White South ended in November 1920. Most of the indexed decade belongs to the Crimean ASSR inside the Russian SFSR and USSR.
Simferopol, Sevastopol, and Kerch are inside; every tested Don, Kuban, Donbas, lower Volga, North Caucasus, and Odesa comparator is outside.
The 1930 white-russia replacement is an atlas-wide error. Crimea and all sampled Soviet points return to ussr by 1938.
Crimean evidence is differentiated by ethnicity, language, faith, class, gender, age, ecology, settlement type, and access to institutions.
Terror, famine, repression, collectivization, dispossession, and disease are treated soberly; humor appears only in safe ordinary-life contexts.
